summary.title: Creating a Roguelike Game in C#
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build a basic roguelike game in C# using the RogueSharp library with MonoGame, RLNet, or SadConsole.
keywords: build your own game in c#
takeaways: RogueSharp is a .NET library for building roguelike games, with tutorials for MonoGame, RLNet, and SadConsole.
The RLNet tutorial series covers project setup, map drawing, player input, map generation, hallways, monsters, combat, scheduling, doors, and stairs.
The MonoGame series covers map generation, field-of-view, exploring the map, pathfinding, a 2D camera, and combat.
Release notes describe library features such as dice notation, goal maps, .NET Standard support, and weighted pools.
The full sample game code is available for RLNet, and the library docs are on the wiki and NuGet.
summary.summary: This blog is a set of tutorials on using the RogueSharp library to create a basic roguelike game in C#. Tutorial series are organized by rendering target: RLNet (the most detailed, covering project setup through stairs), MonoGame (six parts from map generation to combat), and SadConsole, plus a v4 sample ported to Unity. The page also lists release notes for RogueSharp versions 1.1 through 5.0 and a few general .NET posts. The tutorials aim to introduce the library's most commonly used features.
